title: Render a tree as JavaScript
description: You can read visitor methods that format each node using JavaScript syntax.

steps.description: Visitor dispatches on the node class. The example tree binds x to 3 around multiplication followed by addition.
Numbers and variables become source text. Binary operations receive parentheses, with division wrapped in Math.trunc.

steps.question: How does this visitor express a Let binding in JavaScript?
steps.answer: It emits an arrow function and immediately calls it with the binding's value.

steps.description: IfExpr uses a ternary expression. FuncDef emits an arrow function, and Call formats function application.
The displayed generated code is ((x) => ((x * 2) + 1))(3). The browser-console check is a comment; the snippet prints JavaScript without executing it.
